target_customer: Pharma and research labs needing tissue models, long term transplant patients; partners such as United Therapeutics
problem: Engineered human tissue and organs require building vascularized, multicellular structures that existing bioprinters cannot make fast enough. Volumetric builds living tissue for lab testing and drug development with a long term aim of organ replacement.
business_model: Biofabrication technology and tissue products for research and drug development; no revenue model confirmed in sources

founders.name: Jordan Miller
founders.background_notes: YC page lists his degrees; 3dprintingindustry and Rice coverage describe him as an associate professor at Rice.

founders.name: Bagrat Grigoryan
founders.background_notes: YC page gives title only; a news summary calls him a Rice grad student and later 3D Systems VP of regenerative medicine.

competitors.name: CELLINK
competitors.what: Commercial bioprinters and bioinks for research and drug discovery
competitors.traction_then: Announced a liver organoid collaboration with AstraZeneca in May 2020

competitors.name: United Therapeutics with 3D Systems
competitors.what: Collaboration since 2017 on printing a lung scaffold
competitors.traction_then: United projected organ manufacturing about 12 years away in 2018 coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: Printing vascularized living tissue at organ scale is research grade, spanning bioengineering, light based printing and cell biology.

defensibility.rationale: Spin out from a university lab with patents and deep scientific know how; few teams could replicate the biology and engineering.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: 3D Systems acquired the company in October 2021 for up to 400 million dollars with 45 million paid at closing.

market_need_then: The YC page frames demand as human tissue for lab testing and drug development and long term organ replacement, and United Therapeutics was already working with 3D Systems on printed lungs in 2018 coverage.

branding.domain_note: volumetricbio.com; now redirects to a 3D Systems page.

rebrands.to: Volumetric Biotechnologies as a 3D Systems unit
rebrands.why: Absorbed after acquisition; the site redirects to 3D Systems

brand_strength.rationale: A technical brand known mainly in the bioprinting community, and the acquisition coverage focuses on Jordan Miller rather than the brand.

outcome_analysis: Volumetric was a Rice University spin out with research grade technology that attracted 3D Systems, which already worked with United Therapeutics on lung printing. The 400 million dollar headline price is mostly contingent: 45 million at closing and 355 million tied to milestones in human applications, so the realized value is far lower. Success rested on the technical moat and academic founder, and the buyer took the team and Houston facility.
notes: Deal announced October 27, 2021 and expected to close in Q4 2021; closing was not confirmed in sources. The amount_usd field holds the headline maximum, of which 45 million was upfront and half of consideration paid in stock. A 2 million dollar seed in November 2019 appears only on an aggregator and funding totals conflict across aggregators (200 thousand, 1.8 million), so no round is recorded. Rice is described as the origin in news snippets. The 2018 competitor source is a market overview, not specific to Volumetric. Bagrat Grigoryan education unknown. Added a 2M seed announced 2019-11-01 that rests on a single database (StartupIntros page opened; it lists many investors of doubtful accuracy, so only Y Combinator is recorded). Another aggregator dates a seed 2020-08 with no amount; totals conflict.
